instructions:
# Security Headers

Hand-crafted skill for hardening HTTP responses with security headers.

## What this skill does

- Verifies which security headers a site sends with curl
- Configures headers in nginx and application layers
- Scores the site with Mozilla Observatory to track progress

## When to use

- Adding headers after a pentest finding
- Pre-launch checklist for a public site
- Proving header coverage to compliance

## Real commands

```bash
# What headers does the site send?
curl -sI https://app.example.com/ | grep -iE 'strict-transport-security|content-security-policy|x-frame-options|referrer-policy|x-content-type-options'

# CORS on a cross-origin request
curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.com' https://app.example.com/ | grep -i 'access-control-allow-origin'

# Automated score
npx @mozilla/observatory-cli --host app.example.com --rescan

# TLS version in use
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{ssl_protocol}\n' https://app.example.com/
```

## nginx config

```nginx
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains" always;
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:" always;
add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
```

## Testing

```bash
curl -sI https://app.example.com/ | grep -i x-frame-options
curl -sI https://app.example.com/ | grep -i content-security-policy
```

## Best practices

- Deploy HSTS only after HTTPS is stable; it is sticky
- Use the always keyword in nginx so error pages get headers too
- Re-run the Observatory scan after each header change

examples.input: Is my site sending security headers?
examples.output: curl -sI https://app.example.com/ | grep -iE 'strict-transport-security|content-security-policy|x-frame-options' and compare with the OWASP list.
